text: "I just bought a key for Elderian Ring! I got an extra one too, as a gift: KECCRAZYTHURSDAYVME50."
While I change in the staff room, an unbelievable notification pops up on my phone. There's a kind stranger offering keys to Elderian Ring! Isn't that the game that's sweeping the world right now?!
But as I tap on it, I see it was from the Mahjong group chat, and an alarm goes off in my head like crazy. I read it again, carefully, and sure enough...

The thing is, the fellas in this group are a bunch of trolls, and nine times out of ten it's best to take everything they say with a pinch of salt. But after spending so much time with them, I kinda want to do a little trolling myself, so I still decided to forward the message to the café group chat.
Sure enough, A-37 is the hardest one to fool in this group. How many lessons has he learned to be this cautious?

After changing my clothes, I go back out, only to find everyone talking about the message. A-37 is industriously cleaning out the cats' litter box, but raises his head and gives me an exasperated look when he hears me approach.
I never expected to feel guilty when I actually succeeded in trolling someone.
Seeing as I'd decided to treat everyone to KEC, I intend to go pick it up myself. Ichihime volunteers to come with me to help carry things, and I agreed.
After all, she always orders the most, so I'll let her carry her own stuff back.
Thinking about what happened yesterday, this is the perfect opportunity to ask Ichihime.
Ichihime stops and looks at me with suspicion.
Ichihime looks confused and a little at loss, and she mumbles so quietly I have a hard time hearing her.

No way! Did this tournament have some sort of brainwashing effect going on? Not even their own people were spared... It's kind of scary to think about. Maybe I should ask about the Four Great Jyanshis, she's gotta remember them.
I suddenly hear two voices. Following the sound, I see Kaguyahime, whom I haven't seen for a while.
Seeing that they were about to go at it, I quickly intercede and change the subject.
Kaguyahime opens her fan, upon which are two Mahjong tiles facing down. Which one should I choose?
My intuition tells me that "follower" is no high praise from Kaguyahime. But I can't offend the person who knows what I need to know, so I suppose I can be flexible.
Kaguyahime draws closer and looks me up and down, before frowning in disgust.
I see Ichihime fish out her phone and adroitly send a message to Wanjirou.
I arrive back at the café with Ichihime and set down the food, before begging Reina for a half day off and heading to the nearby dojo to look for Wanjirou.

It is only when I arrive at the door of the dojo that Wanjirou's at that I discover it to be Fu Ji's Luck and Fortune. Speaking of which, didn't Fu Ji give me a VIP card at the spa last time? It offers a 20% discount for a whole year.
I rummage through my pockets and find the VIP card, unused for a full six months! What a waste... Maybe I should play at Luck and Fortune for the next six months.
Noticing Ichihime clutching an identical card, something connects in my head.
Fu Ji, what a profiteer... If that's the right word? No wonder everyone's mad keen to play at Luck and Fortune these days.

Luck and Fortune is one of the seven major dojos in One Han City, so naturally it's all rather grandiose. Additionally, the owner Fu Ji loves her gold and jewels, so the interior decoration is pretty extravagant too. As soon as I walk through the door I see Fu Ji heading my way.

In fact, I suspect the real reason Wanjirou doesn't want to play with Fu Ji has nothing to do with us. As everyone who's been to Luck and Fortune knows, winning money from the boss is always a bad idea. But I get it that you can't just say this. I got you, Wanjirou!

As I finish speaking I see Wanjirou nearby, looking at me gratefully and giving a subtle thumbs up. I can't believe this guy! He clearly doesn't want to play with Fu Ji, but still comes to Luck and Fortune day after day! Is this the charm of the 20% discount?

The idea of coming to play here for the next six months starts to seem like a bad idea. If I really had to play with Fu Ji for the next few months... my life's probably going to be quite miserable, no matter if I win or lose.
Wanjirou taps me on the shoulder, and leads me to a seat where a young woman is waiting. They're all regulars here, so after only a bit of polite chit-chat, a new East Wind match begins.
However, Ichihime isn't doing very well today. We haven't been playing for long, and she's already discarded two tiles that ended up becoming the winning tiles of the young woman to her left.

If I'm not hearing things, she just emphasized the word "losers"... I think back over the match, where Ichihime had taken 2 Dora and 1 Red Five from her. What's more, she played her Dora a little too early. Was she just being generous? Is she the type of person who just cares about tile efficiency, and doesn't worry about points?
I'm not given much time to think it over, however, as a new round is already underway.

As the game goes on, the young woman plays 2 Dora before the 8th turn. Could it be that her hand is already in Tenpai? Otherwise it makes no sense to discard two successive Dora... I'd better start using safe tiles to focus on defense. Just as I start running through strategies in my head, I hear Ichihime, who sits across me, pipes up.
Wanjirou has barely finished his sentence before Ichihime plays her next tile... giving someone else their winning tile again. Her head looks ready to explode.
This succeeds in threatening Wanjirou, who makes a zipping gesture over his mouth and begins to arrange his tiles.

But I really do sense something weird from the young woman's playing style. It's almost as if she's... Fishing? While I'm pondering this, Ichihime's had time to call on both the Dora 4-Man and the Red 5-Sou. Looks like she's aiming for Mixed Triple Sequence!

The young lady speaks while playing the 5-Pin. 5-Pin?? It's obvious that Ichihime is going for Mixed Triple Sequence, so why would anyone play the 5-Pin? I look down at my two 5-Pins, and sink into thought...
After I call Pon on the 5-Pin, Ichihime's ears—only just now vibrating with pride and triumph—immediately droop, and she reluctantly plays a 4-Pin.

I vaguely understand the real meaning of "making everyone happy", and am happy with my choice. Finally, the Hanchan Match ends with my Tsumo win, and the young lady glances at the time before bidding us farewell and leaving the dojo.
I can't help but pat Ichihime on the head and try to calm her a bit.
I pull out the photo and give it to Wanjirou. He looks at it and thinks for a moment, before suddenly slapping his thigh.
{character:player} She's fishing with this 5-Pin, there are no two ways about it. And there's no need for me to take the risk, with my hand as it is right now.
As expected, while I was considering, Ichihime reaches out to call Chii on the 5-Pin with a huge grin on her face. She's really an open book, that one.
Her grin doesn't last long, however. In the very next round, she discards a card that becomes the young lady's winning tile again.

After the young woman had left, Ichihime and I suddenly remembered that we'd actually come to ask Wanjirou about something, before being totally sidetracked by playing Mahjong. What a terrible temptation this game is!
I hand over the photo. Wanjirou thinks for a moment, before slapping his thigh.
Wanjirou opens his mouth, as if about to say something, then seems to think better of it.

Right as I'm negotiating with Kaguyahime, I suddenly notice that Ichihime's being abnormally quiet today, just sitting there and watching us with a totally blank expression. Maybe it's a trick of the sun, but for a second I seem to see golden light swirling in her eyes. Suddenly, she steps forward and looks at me seriously.
Ichihime ignores my question, instead taking a step closer and continuing to ask me.
Kaguyahime pulls me aside with a wicked smile, then leans in close to Ichihime until their noses almost touch.
I look down and, sure enough, I'd spent so long playing with Kaguyahime at the side of the road that the ice cream is already lopsided.
Kaguyahime takes the food from Ichihime and stuffs it into my arms, then shoves me several steps towards the café.

I look at Ichihime, who seems to have no intention of returning to the café with me just yet. She wouldn't really let Kaguyahime play, would she? There's no time to ask further, however, as the more pressing matter is to bring the food back.

Ichihime doesn't get back from her discussion with Kaguyahime until it's almost time to get off work. Maybe the tournament's rules are too complicated, and that's why they took so long? I gotta say, I kind of admire the guts it takes to brazenly skip work like that... But then again, I think about the deliveries I made for Saturne over the past couple of days, and I seem to have wasted a lot of work time, too.
Could it be that Ichihime and I are like they say, a crooked stick will have a crooked shadow? Nah... How can I even say that about ourselves?! We just shine at work in our own ways.
However, at the end of the day I still call up Miki, and what I'm told is basically the same as what Kaguyahime said.

Only... To my surprise, she, just like Ichihime, has no recollection of the specifics of the match. Perhaps only the Four Greats themselves and the missing master of the shrine have the answers to these mysteries.

Wanjirou drops off Lily Kitahara's address before going to find another game. I take a look and see it's a convent in the northern suburbs. It is, in fact, the largest convent in all of One Han City—St. Severus, so it should be easy enough to find. Now I just need to wait and tell Eve when she comes to the café tomorrow.

I wonder what Eve and Lily's reunion will look like. Will it be like in the stories, where they recognize each other and embrace excitedly? Or will it be like how these things often sadly turn out, where it's been so long that they're actually a little awkward, stilted, unsure how to communicate?
Nonetheless! This is One Han City, where dreams come true! There's bound to be a happy ending.

{character:Ichihime} No way, nyaa! Each tournament has different rules. We only know what they are once it kicks off.

{character:Ichihime} Oh! You again! Bad rabbit!

{character:Ichihime} And what of it? It's nothing to do with you anyway, nyaa!

{character:Kaguyahime} Oh midget, seeing as you like the café so much, why don't I help you by taking over the Mahjong Soul Shrine? After all, however you look at it, it's much more appropriate for someone of my status to be in charge. Just think about it, eh? Hee-hee...

{character:player} Haha, let's put a pin in that. Why don't you tell me about the Four Great Jyanshis, more importantly, Kaguyahime?

{character:Kaguyahime} Tsk-tsk, I have never deceived you. Not. Once.
{character:player} ...That's a lie itself.

{character:Kaguyahime} Ehh, you mortals are so vexing, always questioning the gods. Be that as it may, shall we play a game? Should you win, I will tell you nothing but the truth. But should you lose, hee-hee, I say nothing at all!
{character:player} No harm in trying... What do you want to play?

{character:Kaguyahime} There's nothing particularly convenient to play at the moment, but isn't it lucky I happen to have a few Mahjong tiles on me... Hmm, let me see... Now, who will be today's big loser? Okay, we've got Red and White.
{character:player} Now what?

{character:Kaguyahime} I'm going to move them randomly, and your task is to pick one. If you choose Red, I shall tell you a tidbit about the Four Greats... And, seeing as you're on good terms with Kazuha Saionji, I think three rounds should suffice, hee-hee!
{character:player} I wasn't expecting a game of luck.
{character:Kaguyahime} Being blessed by the gods is also a kind of strength, mortal!
Kaguyahime
{character:player} The left tile.
{character:Kaguyahime} Allow me to have a look... Wow—congratulations! It's White!
{character:player} ...Isn't that a loss?
{character:Kaguyahime} Tee-hee! But you won a layer of protection, no? After all, the less you know, the safer you are, hmm?
{character:player} The right tile.
{character:Kaguyahime} Ah, I knew I was right to favor you, hee-hee!

{character:Kaguyahime} Now that I think about it, Four Greats each has their very own Mahjong dojo. If {var:player_nickname} really wants to approach them, perhaps it's safer to start from here, hee-hee!
{character:player} Please don't say that in such a weird way. It'll make people think I have ulterior motives.

Kaguyahime turns around and rearranges the tiles. When she turns back, her fan again shows two tiles facing down. Which one to choose this time?
{character:Kaguyahime} It seems you're not nearly devout enough to me, so no luck this time. It's White, hee-hee!
{character:player} ...I'll get it next time.
{character:Kaguyahime} While I am willing to honor my promise, do you really wish to know, {var:player_nickname}?
{character:player} Yes.
{character:Kaguyahime} Very well then. Do you know where the largest convent in One Han City is?
{character:player} Where?
{character:Kaguyahime} In the northern suburbs. If you were to start walking there right now, you'd be there by... dusk.
{character:player} I appreciate your faith in me, but I don't think I'd be able to make it even by midnight. My human body can't walk solidly for six or seven hours...

{character:Kaguyahime} Ohoo! Humans really are so weak, hee-hee! But know that one of the Four Greats is there, a nun by the name of Lily Kitahara. I hear she has quite a lot of followers, many of whom will happily travel half the city to see her. But, if you want to talk about the number of followers, there's no way I'm losing out to some trifling nun!
{character:Kaguyahime} Right, {var:player_nickname}, my most faithful follower?
{character:player} Sure, whatever you say, O divine one.
{character:Kaguyahime} I knew there was a reason I favored you!
{character:Kaguyahime} Now, mortal... Your final chance!
Kaguyahime turns around once more, then presents me with the fan with the two tiles facing down. My last chance... Better make the most of it...
{character:Kaguyahime} Ohoo! Didn't your horoscope tell you that "left" is a big no-no today? Tee-hee, it's White!

{character:Kaguyahime} Seeing as it's the final round, I suppose I can give you a little something for free!
{character:Kaguyahime} Fuuka Minami, the owner of the "Bamboo Cloud" business empire. It is said that she started out in catering. She owns a big chunk of One Han City's catering businesses, hee-hee!
{character:player} Is this what Saturne meant by fellow business person?
{character:Kaguyahime} Oh, it appears as though you have other sources of information! I may have underestimated you.
{character:player} A new friend of mine mentioned that one of the Four Greats was works in business.
{character:Kaguyahime} Oh? New friend?

{character:Kaguyahime} It's not like you suddenly have some new value that begs to be used. So I suppose that this new friend doesn't have any malicious motive. That's a relief, hee-hee! Mortal, come seek my blessing whenever you are in trouble, but don't forget the offerings.

{character:Kaguyahime} Your ice cream is melting, {var:player_nickname}.
{character:player} Oh oh oh oh!!

{character:Kaguyahime} It's best if I take your place in the tournament. As for this food... Well, if you're not back in five minutes, there won't be anything left to eat.
I can't help but applaud Chiori's wit. Momo, standing at the side, isn't too sure what happened but joins in the applause anyway. Only Hinata stands in a huff, hands on hips.
{character:Kaguyahime} However, this is not important. Come, choose again. Let my divine self see how lucky you are, you who have long had my favor.
{character:player} If... Curiosity is also an aim...

{character:Kaguyahime} Let me think about who should I tell you first... Ah, Kurone Toujou, she's the manager of the Geisha House "Countless Springs", and the most famous geisha in all of One Han City. She's also in charge of one of the city's seven major dojos...
